claims.location: comment[cleavage agent details] all rows
claims.evidence: mzid Enzyme name='Trypsin' MS:1001251, missedCleavages=2, semiSpecific=false. 93.9% and 92.9% of peptide sequences in two sampled Peptide chunks (488 and 479 peptides) end in K/R. The PRIDE prose names FASP but not the enzyme (reconcile flagged this). The cited FASP protocol (Wisniewski 2013) uses Lys-C followed by trypsin, so a Lys-C pre-digestion cannot be ruled out. Neither the PRIDE protocol nor the deposited search names Lys-C; trypsin is supported by the mzid enzyme and the K/R C-termini.

claims.evidence: Patient 48 is outside the published 11-patient analysis. PRIDE and the abstract describe 11 patients, and Landolt 2017 Table 1 marks exactly 18, 21, 22, 27, 29, 31, 33, 39, 44, 46, 53 with P (proteomics). Landolt 2017 Methods: 'Two additional patients were excluded because of a mixture of carcinoma and normal tissue in the respective biopsies.' Patient 48 is likely one of these (unconfirmed). The T/N suffix shows the intended biopsy site only, not confirmed histology or purity, so no diagnosis is asserted. T/N stays visible in the source and assay names. This matches the handling of excluded patients in sibling Bergen dataset PXD010260. Changed after the second independent review.

limitations: Full text of the primary paper (PMID 30838877) was not retrievable (publisher HTTP 403, no PMC/repository copy); only abstract, MeSH and the PRIDE protocols were used for it.

Patient-to-file mapping and per-patient age/sex/tumour size come from three related papers by the same group sharing one patient numbering; the proteomics paper itself was not read to confirm the numbering.

Patient 48 (2 RAW files) appears in no published table; the primary paper reports 11 patients, so patient 48 may have been excluded from the published analysis. Patient 48 is outside the published 11-patient analysis and is likely one of the two patients Landolt 2017 excluded for mixed carcinoma/normal biopsies (unconfirmed). Both files are kept because they are genuine deposited runs. Disease, factor value, demographics and tumour size are 'not available' on rows 11 and 23; T/N (intended biopsy site) appears only in the source and assay names.
Lys-C pre-digestion (as in the cited Wisniewski 2013 FASP protocol) cannot be ruled out; only trypsin is annotated, per the deposited search.
Fuhrman grade and stage differ between the group's papers for some patients (e.g. patient 44 Fuhrman 2 vs 4; patient 18 stage III vs 2), so tumour grade/stage were not annotated.

The deposited mzid is a SearchGUI/PeptideShaker search of 30 Progenesis-exported MGFs; the PRIDE data protocol describes a Proteome Discoverer 1.4 search with fewer variable modifications. Modifications follow the deposited PeptideShaker mzid rather than the published Proteome Discoverer search.
Cell type and ancestry are not reported per sample (not available).
